🐛 Bug
The implementation of kl_div in torch.nn.functional seems to have numerical problems. It can output negative kl divergence, and small numbers even though they should be zero. The problem could be due to the fact that it accepts input as log_probability while the target as probability.

To Reproduce
Suppose we have two outputs of the same values:
a = torch.tensor([[1.0,2,3], [5.0, 5.0, 5.0]])
b = torch.tensor([[1.0,2,3], [5.0, 5.0, 5.0]])
The output of the kl divergence according to the Pytorch implementation is:
F.kl_div(F.log_softmax(a, 1), F.softmax(b, 1), reduction="none")
tensor([[-6.8829e-09, -1.4331e-08, -6.4222e-08], [ 1.6545e-08,  1.6545e-08,  1.6545e-08]])
Expected behavior
A simple implementation like below gives the correct behaviour, although probably not a very optimised implementation.
F.softmax(b, dim=1) * (F.log_softmax(b, dim=1) - F.log_softmax(a, dim=1))
tensor([[0., 0., 0.], [0., 0., 0.]])
cc @ezyang @gchanan @zou3519

Nested RecordFunctions during profiling do not work with RPC calls, due to mismanagement of some internal variables in record_function.cpp caused by handling RecordFunction objects completing in different hreads.
To Reproduce
with torch.autograd.profiler.profiler() as prof:
    with torch.autograd.profiler.record_function("foo"):
        rpc.rpc_async(...)

will result in an error:
> I0122 16:32:15.967217 594065 record_function.cpp:214] Exception in RecordFunction::end(): (thread_local_func_ == thi
s) || (thread_local_func_ == nullptr && threadId_ != 0) INTERNAL ASSERT FAILED at caffe2/torch/csrc/autograd/record_fu
nction.cpp:235, please report a bug to PyTorch. baze: must be top of stack. If you are calling RecordFunction::end in
aseparate thread, call RecordFunction::setThreadId() in the creatingthread. (end at caffe2/torch/csrc/autograd/record_

🚀 Feature
Option to provide a seed (random_state) for random_split() like the sklearn API https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.model_selection.train_test_split.html.
Motivation
Useful for deterministic sampling & reproducible data generation (easily, without affecting the PRNG for other uses).
Pitch / implementation proposal
In dataset.py
+ from torch.random import manual_seed, get_rng_state, set_rng_state

-def random_split(dataset, lengths):
+def random_split(dataset, lengths, random_state=None):
    r"""
    Randomly split a dataset into non-overlapping new datasets of given lengths.

    Arguments:
        dataset (Dataset): Dataset to be split
        lengths (sequence): lengths of splits to be produced
+       random_state (int, optional): seed used by the random number generator
    """
    if sum(lengths) != len(dataset):
        raise ValueError("Sum of input lengths does not equal the length of the input dataset!")

+   if random_state is not None:
+       state = get_rng_state()
+       manual_seed(random_state)

    indices = randperm(sum(lengths)).tolist()
-   return [Subset(dataset, indices[offset - length:offset]) for offset, length in zip(_accumulate(lengths), lengths)]
+   splits = [Subset(dataset, indices[offset - length:offset]) for offset, length in zip(_accumulate(lengths), lengths)]
+   if random_state is not None:
+       set_rng_state(state)
+   return splits
It could also allow a ByteTensor to be compatible with get_rng_state().
Alternatives
Manually call manual_seed() before splitting, without forgetting to save and restore the state with get/set_rng_state() or with fork_rng() (by the way it's not obvious from the docs that it should used with with, maybe add a snippet?)

🐛 Bug
When spawning multiple processes (e.g. for training models on different GPUs for hyperparameter search) that have their own dataloader with pin_memory = True and where the model uses torch.cat(), multiple CUDA contexts are created on the first GPU.
To Reproduce
Execute following code sample and play with use_cat and pin_memory variables. If you set one of these to False, no additional context is created on GPU 0.
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.multiprocessing as mp
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader, Dataset

ctx = mp.get_context("spawn")

class RandomSet(Dataset):

    def __getitem__(self, item):
        return torch.randn(256,256,256)

    def __len__(self):
        return 1000


class CatModel(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, use_cat=True):
        super(CatModel, self).__init__()

        self.use_cat = use_cat

        if use_cat:
            self.conv = nn.Conv2d(512, 512, 3)
        else:
            self.conv = nn.Conv2d(256, 512, 3)

    def forward(self, x):

        if self.use_cat:
            x = torch.cat([x, x], dim=1)

        return self.conv(x)


# change either one to False: No additional CUDA context created

pin_memory = True

class Trainer(ctx.Process):
    def __init__(self, device):
        super(Trainer, self).__init__()

        self.device = device

        self.dataset = RandomSet()
        self.dataloder = DataLoader(
            self.dataset,
            pin_memory=pin_memory,
            batch_size=8,
            num_workers=8

    def run(self):

    trainer2 = Trainer(1)

This is a follow-up task to #24132
Background
About 25% of our operators are currently using the new templated mechanism for unboxing operators when they're called from a boxed world like JIT or Mobile. The other 75% still use the old mechanism where we run a Python codegen script to generate the C++ code doing the unboxing. We want to use the templated mechanism everywhere, but there's a few issues we have to fix first.
Note: If an op uses the templated mechanism or the codegen mechanism is determined by the use_c10_dispatcher flag in native_functions.yaml. If it is set to use_c10_dispatcher: full, then it uses the templated mechanism. If it is set to anything else (or if it is missing), then it uses the codegen mechanism.
Gaps
The percentage numbers in parentheses denote how many of our ops are using this feature

 (17%) out functions don't work

 they have different argument order in C++ as in the jit schema (#47711, #47712, #47792, #47793, #48910, #48911, #48912, #49006, #49012)
 they use Tensor& instead of const Tensor& (#42712)


 (9%) Tensor? (i.e. optional tensor) doesn't work nicely with undefined tensor sometimes being undefined tensor and sometimes being None. (#41610, #41947)
 (6%) TensorOptions ops don't work

 They have different dispatch algorithms in the boxed and the unboxed world (#36562)
 They have different runtime representations (packed vs unpacked) in the boxed and the unboxed world (not sure if this is still an issue) (#39492, #39611)
 Backend Select currently doesn't work with use_c10_dispatcher: full because  gen_backend_select_register.py doens't support it yet (#39492)
 They have different signatures (#39611, #41169)


 Argument types not supported in the function schema inference yet:

 (8%) ScalarType (#39492)
 (6%) Device (#39492)
 (6%) Layout (#39492)
 (1%) Storage (#49146)
 (4%) Generator (#26434)
 (4%) Dimname (#49008)
 (1%) MemoryFormat (#39492)
 (1%) ConstQuantizerPtr (#49150, #49463)


 (15%) Fixed size arrays don't work yet (#34399)
 (14%) ArrayRef arguments don't work, the custom op API expects torch::List. (#34335)
 (1%) Lists of optional tensors (i.e. Tensor?[]) don't work yet (#49138)
 (1%) Optional lists (i.e. Dimname[]?) don't work yet (#49088)
 (14%) Multiple return values work differently
 (4%) Generator is currently a dispatch-relevant argument for unboxed dispatch but boxed dispatch ignores it. This is because it is a JIT type but not an IValue type, so boxed dispatch cannot recognize it. 🐛 Bug
Exporting a function with the same name as a module while also importing anything from that module (not the module as a whole but from module import X) causes a name collision in the exported TorchScript.
It is rather unusual to use the same name as the module, but in case of combining the individual steps into one, it can be reasonable. While this can easily be avoided, it is perfectly acceptable in Python.
Only occurs with PyTorch 1.4.0, older versions worked just fine.
To Reproduce
Consider the example of preprocessing an image before feeding it to the model, the preprocessing logic is in the module preprocess and then a preprocess function is defined to combine the different steps into one pipeline.
preprocess.py
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F


# Resize the bigger side to the given size but keep aspect ratio
def resize(image: torch.Tensor, larger_size: int):
    image = image.unsqueeze(0)
    _, _, height, width = image.size()
    if height >= width:
        new_height = larger_size
        new_width = width * larger_size // height
    else:
        new_width = larger_size
        new_height = height * larger_size // width
    return F.interpolate(image, size=(new_height, new_width), mode="bilinear", align_corners=False).squeeze(0)


# Pad image to be divisible by a given value
def pad(image: torch.Tensor, divisible_by: int, value: float = 0.0):
    _, height, width = image.size()
    effective_height = int(torch.ceil(torch.tensor(height, dtype=torch.float) / divisible_by) * divisible_by)
    effective_width = int(torch.ceil(torch.tensor(width, dtype=torch.float) / divisible_by) * divisible_by)
    return F.pad(
        image,
        [0, effective_width - width, 0, effective_height - height],
        mode="constant",
        value=value,
    )
export.py
import torch
import torch.jit
import torch.nn as nn

from preprocess import pad, resize


# Define a preprocessing function that uses the building blocks of the preprocess module
# Renaming it, fixes the problem
def preprocess(image: torch.Tensor, size: int, divisible_by: int):
    image = resize(image, size)
    image = pad(image, divisible_by)
    return image


class Model(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, size: int = 1024, divisible_by: int = 128):
        super(Model, self).__init__()
        self.size = size
        self.divisible_by = divisible_by

    def forward(self, image):
        image = preprocess(image, self.size, self.divisible_by)

        # Do something with the preprocessed image
        # ...


model = Model()

# Export the model
jit_model = torch.jit.script(model)
jit_model.save("model.pth")

# Load the model later
loaded_model = torch.jit.load("model.pth")

    divisible_by: int) -> Tensor:
  image1 = __torch__.preprocess.resize(image, size, )

🚀 Feature

I would request to add an Alltoall / alltoallv communication primitive to torch.distributed module and corresponding implementations to MPI, GLOO and other distributed backends.
Motivation
When using both data and model parallelism in modern workloads (such as DLRM), communication pattern required for switching from one type of parallelism to other maps very well to all-to-all communication well studied in HPC workloads. MPI provides MPI_Alltoall (and more flexible MPI_Alltoallv APIs to perform this type of communication). In absence of alltoall support, we nee to use sequence of gathers or scatters to perform same communication. Having alltoall API allows reducing number of calls required to communication backend and avoid redundant data copies.
DLRM Research Paper explains this communication pattern as butterfly-shuffle in its Parallelism section.

Pitch
Suppose we have 4 processes and each one has one input tensor with following data:
input:
[ 0  1  2  3]  # Proc 0
[ 4  5  6  7]  # Proc 1
[ 8  9 10 11]  # Proc 2
[12 13 14 15]  # Proc 3

After the communication, we want following output tensor on each processes:
output:
[ 0  4  8 12]  # Proc 0
[ 1  5  9 13]  # Proc 1
[ 2  6 10 14]  # Proc 2
[ 3  7 11 15]  # Proc 3

So, we simply call:
data = [ rank * 4 + i for i in range(4)]
input = torch.tensor(data)
output = torch.empty_like(input)
dist.alltoall(output, input)

This will split the input tensor equally and scatter to all the processes. On the other hand, output tensor would be split equally and receive gathered tensors from respective process.
Alternatively, if we have list of tensors to scatter and gather list for receiving tensors or we explicitly want to specify what portion goes where (particularly, in multi-dimensional tensor), we can explicitly pass list of tensors as scatter_list and gather_list:
scatter_list = list(input.split(1))
gather_list = list(output.split(1))
dist.alltoall(gather_list, scatter_list)

Alternatives
Today, doing it with scatter would require this:
scatter_list = list(input.split(1))
gather_list = list(output.split(1))
for i in range(4):
    dist.scatter(gather_list[i], scatter_list if i == rank else [], src = i)

nodes.bodyText:
The derivative of a linear function is constant, and so the second derivative is zero.
Trying to replicate these derivatives in pytorch fails, because the first gradient does not get a grad_fn.
This will make a straight forward implementation of the second derivative fail for linear functions, while working fine for non-linear functions.
To Reproduce
Here is a basic implementation of the second derivative for functions with scalar input and output.
def second_deriv(y, x):
    # first derivative of scalar y = f(x) wrt scalar x
    first = torch.autograd.grad(y, x, create_graph=True)[0]
    # second derivative of y wrt x
    second = torch.autograd.grad(first, x, create_graph=True)[0]
    return second
For non-linear functions this works just as expected.
>>> x = torch.tensor(1.0, requires_grad=True)
>>> second_deriv(x**2, x)
tensor(2., grad_fn=<MulBackward0>)
However, for linear functions the second derivative fails. The reason is that in second_deriv, the tensor first doesn't have a grad_fn.
>>> second_deriv(x*2, x)
RuntimeError: element 0 of tensors does not require grad and does not have a grad_fn

Expected behavior
I would expect the gradient to always get a grad_fn when retain_graph=True, even if it is just a trivial dependence (i.e. no actual dependence) on input variables as in the linear case.
One can manually work around this by checking if grad_fn == None for the first gradient.
Any algorithm using higher derivatives could then manually create zero tensors as required.
However, in this case at least the documentation should be amended to mention that the presence of a gradient function is not guaranteed.
It seems to me that an implementation of my expected behavior is essentially just a Function  producing a zero tensor as gradient based on the shape of input variables.
Since I suspect this is an issue few people will notice when using pytorch, I can't decide if the increase in code is worth it.
Environment
The described behavior appears in all pytorch versions I have used, including 1.3.1.
cc @ezyang @ssnl @albanD @zou3519 @gqchen

nodes.title: PyTorch android not working with Progaurd and minified enabled in release mode android.

nodes.bodyText:
🐛 Bug
I trained a model on my desktop and then traced it and converted it using torch.jit.trace() function to use it on mobile phone(android). It is working fine when the app is in debug mode on android. But when I use Proguard and enable minified and create apk in release mode it is not working (means apk is not successfully made) and I get an error
To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

Train any model on desktop or laptop.
Set it to eval mode and trace it using torch.jit.trace() function and save it to a ".pt' file.
Use PyTorch Android 1.3.0 and load the model on your android app.
Create .apk for your app with ProGuard enabled and Minified enbaled, you'll get this error.

🐛 Bug

The Torchscript engine in Pytorch compiles the model, but fails to run it due to a library error.
To Reproduce

Run the below file

import torch
class TensorConstant(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, value):
        # type: (Tensor) -> None
        super(TensorConstant, self).__init__()
        self.val = torch.tensor(value)

    def forward(self, xs):
        # type: (Tuple[Dict[str,Tensor], Dict[str, Tensor]]) -> Tensor
        reals, bools = xs
        return self.val

class Real(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, name):
        super(Real, self).__init__()
        self.name = name

    def forward(self, xs):
        # type: (Tuple[Dict[str,Tensor], Dict[str, Tensor]]) -> Tensor
        reals, bools = xs
        return reals[self.name]

class Minus(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, f1, f2):
        super(Minus, self).__init__()
        self.f1 = f1
        self.f2 = f2

    def forward(self, xs):
        # type: (Tuple[Dict[str,Tensor], Dict[str, Tensor]]) -> Tensor
        val = self.f1.forward(xs) - self.f2.forward(xs)
        return val

xs = ({'foo': torch.tensor(1.0, requires_grad=True)}, {})
f1 = TensorConstant(2.0)
f2 = Real("foo")
model = Minus(f1, f2)
